item.title: 139. An Unsexy Spirituality
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: A single true sentence gave me the strength I needed. The rock, or the tide of emotions? The rock, or the flames of passion? The rock, or the lightning of…
item.content:encoded:
The rock, or the tide of emotions?
The rock, or the flames of passion?
The rock, or the lightning of inspiration?
If I must walk every day, let it be on rock.

In my letter "132. To Row, or Not to Row," I told how a spectacular unblocking had taken place in my solar plexus, the center related to doing and to "I can." I uncovered a belief I had been holding for several years: that effort comes from the ego; in God, everything unfolds with ease and inspiration.

I'm not saying it is false or true; it is limited, and that limitation was like a rope binding my wings. What beliefs do is tell God how reality should be. That is why, if you want to know reality, you have to let go of all beliefs.

When I let go of that one, enormous changes happened in my life. I now get done in a day what used to take me a week. Now the problem is that I find it hard to stop!

I have also discovered the supreme importance of developing character. I used to confuse it with the ego; why put so much effort into improving what is fleeting? Now I see more clearly what it is: virtues do not live in the same dimension as the vices of character, just as the sky does not live in the same dimension as the clouds, or light in the same dimension as shadows. It is not about improving what is fleeting, but about letting it go so that what is eternal can shine. To truly integrate spirituality and be able to do God's will on Earth as it is in Heaven, the development of character is central.

What I love about this shift in perspective is, first, how unsexy it is. I used to think liberation lay in seeking something ideal: always working inspired, always letting a voice beyond the clouds tell me what the next thing to do was. Now I simply try to do what I have to do. And that, which I once would have felt as oppressive, is now tremendously freeing, because my action no longer depends on my fluctuating, capricious moods, or on my personal likes and dislikes. It now depends on truth, and it seeks the good simply because it is good.

A few days after this awakening, this wonderful triptych came to me, mentioned almost in passing in a book by Romano Guardini. When I heard it, I knew it was my new true north:

What is, is.
What is right must be done.
What has been entrusted to me, I uphold.

I felt the power of truth in those words when, the next day, I spent several hours cleaning the terrace, something I had been avoiding for weeks. A single true sentence gave me the strength I needed: “What is right must be done.”

What I love about this shift in perspective is, second, that it is filling me with hope. And I recognize it for what it is, a theological virtue, a light I cannot make on my own: a gift from God. The gift is looking to the future and no longer seeing my past mistakes repeating themselves, my projected guilt coming back at me like rabid dogs, my limitations hurting me and those I love: now I look to the future and see, behind the opaque curtain of the unknown, a tender smile.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 138. Life Doesn't Know Death
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: When poets celebrate the freedom of birds, they're really talking about the sky. It was night. Muhammet, Betül's brother, and I were looking out in…
item.content:encoded:
It was night. Muhammet, Betül's brother, and I were looking out in silence from the balcony. Hills of concrete and thousands of lit windows stretching toward the horizon in every direction: Istanbul. “Dystopia,” Muhammet said. I nodded, and we lost ourselves in the distance again.

Yesterday Gülistan, Betül’s mother, had surgery. It was a hard day, listening to death drag its pale feet through the hospital corridors.

I was sitting in an armchair, taking the pulse of the room. There was fear, sadness, exhaustion, anger. I still can’t understand a word of Turkish, but I’m fluent in Energy.

I looked out the window and saw a few flocks of birds flying together, having the time of their lives. Then a thought came to me that I had never had before:

Life doesn’t know death.

I was grateful for the gift, a moment worthy of a haiku. In fact, here it is:

Last dance
Between swifts and sky
Dark clouds

That thought mirrored the paradox I had been living all day. We have two overlapping natures: one bound by time and space, the other eternal and infinite.

Swift and sky.

I think that when poets celebrate the freedom of birds, they are really talking about the sky. But since there is little to say about it, we speak of those who know it best.

Jesus and God.

Once you recognize this seemingly dual nature, it becomes clear that death touches only one of them. The other is Life itself.

Then you look at the devastation that is inseparable from this world, and inside, you don’t move, at least not deep down. You look at it and tell it: you are not real, and you cannot touch me, at least not deep down.

This is not intellectual, it is not a belief. Before that thought arrived, “Life doesn’t know death,” what I felt was an unshakable peace in the midst of the dark clouds. An indifference that Saint Ignatius described not as apathy or insensitivity, but as inner freedom. I experienced it as compassion, which says to the one who suffers: I see your suffering, I give it room to be, but I also recognize your freedom.

Fear passed through me yesterday, but it couldn’t grab hold of me and carry me off. My role was a different one: to hold on to that peace and bring it to the surface. The swift is individual, the sky is shared. All it takes is for one swift to cry out “we’re flying!” for all of them to realize the infinity that embraces and holds them.

That is my song today, which I express in these words: Life doesn’t know death!

A few minutes ago, Gülistan came out of intensive care and returned to her room. While her children look after her, I write this, like a seismograph recording spiritual tremors.

I don’t know to what extent Gülistan identifies with the sky she already is. What I do know is that the first words she murmured when she opened her eyes and saw her daughter were: I was with my father and my mother, and we were going to Mecca.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 137. Constant Prayer
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: Consciously or unconsciously, ask and it will be given to you. The other day, a member of the community asked me about how to spend more time praying or…
item.content:encoded:
The other day, a member of the community asked me about how to spend more time praying or being aware of the Presence.

The answer was that, in reality, we are always praying.

Sometimes we pray explicitly, through thoughts or out loud, but we are always doing it implicitly. The mechanism is always on. At every moment, there is some desire or longing in our heart, and that is the constant prayer.

When we pray well, that is, redirecting the longing of the heart toward the true God, we receive what we have asked for: his peace and the memory of his love. However, when we stop praying, our heart returns to its habitual prayers, which tend to be oriented toward the things of this world, things that must be in the future because we do not feel them now. Our prayer then moves from the true God to all kinds of false gods: in our heart we pray to the god of productivity and success, because only he can save us from scarcity and insufficiency. We pray to the god of pleasure, because he will give us the joy we lack right now. We pray to the god of approval, dreaming that he will confirm to us “you are enough, you are good.” We pray to the god of control, so that nothing bad will happen to us.

There are many false gods, and none of them are real. Which means our prayers receive emptiness as a response. External things arrive and soon pass; but the missing puzzle piece in our heart remains not-there.

But the maxim always holds: ask, and it will be given to you.

In every instant, you are receiving the answer to the prayer of your heart. It never fails, it cannot fail. You are seeing what you have asked for.

Do you understand now why all religions place such emphasis on opening the heart? If we never go in there to put things in order, it will be the disorder that raises its prayer, and disorder is what we will receive in return.

If you put God second, you put him nowhere.

The ultimate goal of prayer is to learn to ask only for the peace of God.

Saint Augustine said that happiness consists in desiring only what is good, and having all our desires fulfilled.

One could debate endlessly about what is good, but the second part of the Doctor’s phrase gives us a clue: how can we always have all our desires fulfilled? It can only be if what we desire is always present, always given, and merely waiting to be accepted.

That is why the conclusion I reach is this: there is nothing outside this instant that I truly want to desire.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 136. Ángeles
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: Help always comes. The story of Nimbo is full of moments where the most gracious Providence made itself known. Here is one of them.
item.content:encoded:
The story of Nimbo is full of moments where the most gracious Providence made itself known. Here is one of them.

It was late March and there were four souls on the beach. In one hand I carried my hulking camera with its enormous tripod, in the other a beach bag with a mirror, water, and other items that turned out to be useless, my guitar over my shoulder, and dressed as if going to an Indian wedding. Naturally, my ego was walking behind me, kicking me in the butt and throwing sand in my hair. I felt alone and a little ridiculous, but I knew I had a mission, so I pressed on with a firm-clumsy step across the sand.

I set the camera in the exact spot where the Will wanted it, facing the approaching sunset, and stood in front of it to play Nimbo.

I had not reached the second chorus when I saw a woman approaching with a warm smile. I do not think she realized I was recording, because she walked into the frame and stood there watching me play, inaudibly beneath the sound of the sea. “Well, this take is not the one...” I laughed, and started talking to her.

She told me she had come over because she had felt the light that was with me. She told me she was in Cantabria those days looking for a premises for Cáritas. Her name was Ángeles, and in her smile I saw Christ coming to help me.

I explained that I was filming a music video and invited her to join. She agreed with delight, although she was sorry not to be better dressed. I told her she was perfect: with that scarf on her head like a turban and her walking stick she looked like a biblical shepherd. I filmed several shots of her alone, smiling at the camera, and finally joined the frame to play Nimbo for her. When the second-to-last verse arrived, I felt that instead of singing I should hug her, and that is what I did. And so the heart of the video was captured.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 135. One structure breaks, a higher one forms
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: How marriage, and other changes, have been changing my identity. In the space of a month, I have gotten married, started releasing my songs, and…
item.content:encoded:
In the space of a month, I have gotten married, started releasing my songs, and half-moved to Istanbul. I have also suddenly understood the importance of character development, which has opened my eyes to that dimension with unusual clarity: ouch.

Let's talk about how to navigate the identity shift that the inevitable changes in circumstance bring with them.

When something ends, whether it was good or not, we humans suffer. We confuse our circumstance with our identity, and when the circumstance ends, the associated identity feels threatened.

An example:

I am now someone's husband. That identity is new, although it has been a slow-burning change. I met Betül three years ago, but I knew I was going to marry her four years ago.

This new identity is so deep that it includes another person within it. It is a change that encompasses my whole being, like someone who becomes a monk.

In the process of becoming Betül's husband, I have experienced the same pattern again and again: my new shared way of life reveals that part of my identity no longer works: the Antonio-lone-wolf, the Antonio-who-doesn't-make-the-bed, the Antonio-who-only-thinks-of-himself, the Antonio-who-lets-himself-be-carried-away-by-melancholy... Blessed be marriage, which calls us to leave those cages behind.

With each of those identities, the same thing happened:

the mirror of the relationship makes me aware of a destructive identity,

I feel shame and guilt,

I project that negativity outward and that makes me feel attacked,

the identity defends itself by justifying itself,

at some point the spiritual alarm goes off: I seek the truth,

I see that what is calling me to change is not only my circumstance, or a beautiful Turkish girl: it is the healing voice of God himself,

I stop projecting my pain,

I take up my cross,

I see that the one carrying it is Christ in me,

I choose to stop crucifying him,

I hand the guilty identity over to the fire of innocence,

tremors in the shadow,

tectonic plates grinding beneath the surface of consciousness,

the light of Christ shines through the clouds,

the trumpets of redemption sound,

calm

something new is born: the Antonio-who-loves-constant-company, the Antonio-who-makes-the-bed-as-prayer, the Antonio-who-remembers-at-the-shop-what-Betül-mentioned-had-run-out, the Antonio-who-chooses-to-pull-himself-free-from-the-dark-hand-of-melancholy-to-bring-hope-into-Betül's-world.

One structure breaks, a higher one forms.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 134. I did it!
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: On the mysterious authorship of Nimbo. Last Friday the Nimbo music video came out. You can watch it by clicking above. To read about its mysterious…
item.content:encoded:
Last Friday the Nimbo music video came out.
You can watch it by clicking above.
To read about its mysterious authorship, keep reading.

Last Friday I published the music video for Nimbo, and I felt the joy of having achieved a great goal. "I did it!" I said to Betül, but immediately something jarred in my mind. If there is one thing I have taken from all these years of spiritual journey, it is that I am not alone, nor do I do anything alone. I corrected myself then, adding:

You did it.

My parents did it.

Ari (the album's producer) did it.

Joe (my teacher) did it.

All my teachers, friends and cousins did it.

The whole universe did it.

Jesus did it.

God did it.

This song represents for me a true fruit of the Spirit, and the Spirit is everything. Antonio is the small branch on which that fruit grew, but it is inseparable from the tree.

It is evident in my experience that neither the song nor the video were my invention.

The song arrived easily in a few minutes, almost without my noticing.

The video was a longer process and therefore left more space for my ego to appear saying lovely things like "I have no idea what I am doing," "you don't even know how to use a camera," or "why do I insist on doing everything alone?"

But just as a photon moves through empty space in a straight line, I move straight through God's seemingly crooked lines.

"I don't know what I'm doing" was overcome by an infinite "Trust in Me, I do."

"I don't know how to use the camera" by a "you know enough."

"Why alone" was constantly dissolved by an "I am here" that reverberated through my entire experience.

When the moment came to edit the video, my ego spoke again: "this makes no sense, there is no concept, these are just disconnected images and most of them have nothing special about them."

I turned then to the one who does know and said: "Lord, I don't know how to do this, you edit it."

The anxiety and frustration dissolved and, in a state of calm, the shots began finding their place, at a slow pace, with spacious frames that reflected the absence of hurry with which the editing was happening.

Finally, I understood what the concept of the video was: the light passing through form, just like the album cover with its Christic tree, and just like the song, with its om sounding through the river, the sun, and you.

Everything was perfectly coherent, in a way I had not been able to see from my perspective as a busy little ant.

For things like these it feels dishonest to say "I did it!" unless in that "I" I include my Lord. In that case, it works.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 133. Nimbo (Halo)
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: The world sings if you like to listen. Last Friday, Nimbo came out, the first single from my new album, Silent Transmission.
item.content:encoded:
Last Friday, Nimbo came out, the first single from my new album, Silent Transmission.

133. Nimbo

Lord, how hard it has been!

I composed it six years ago, and I am not exaggerating when I say that getting here has been an odyssey. A journey into the intimately unknown and back.

Nimbo came out on Friday and, the moment I joined the meditation with the community, I began to cry. I saw, like a film, all the stages of the journey, the hardest moments, and how the light would invariably come to take my soul out of the hands of fear. The rest of the half hour was a meditation on how hope is entirely justified when one walks hand in hand with God. There is no obstacle that can resist Him. What for us is a mountain, for Him is not even a feather.

Afterward, this prayer-poem came to express that (trans)personal journey I had just reviewed, inspired by the traditional Jewish prayer "Dayenu" ("It would have been enough"):

If God had shown me, at 21, that I was his beloved son and that there was nothing to forgive
It would have been enough

If he had taken me off the path of engineering and let me fly in the open field
It would have been enough

If he had given me a single inspired song
It would have been enough

If he had opened my heart and healed the wounds kept there
It would have been enough

If he had sent me a beggar with broken legs lying on the pavement to teach me to see Christ in every man
It would have been enough

If he had brought me a good teacher who taught me that my true will is to know God
It would have been enough

If he had brought me A Course in Miracles to teach me to forgive
It would have been enough

If he had restored love and harmony in my family
It would have been enough

If he had healed my voice after four years of constant pharyngitis
It would have been enough

If he had accompanied me through the hell of healing my relationship with food
It would have been enough

If, in my most painful loneliness, he had called me to marriage, brought me Betül, and fulfilled his promise
It would have been enough

If he had placed me in the hands of Jesus and taught me to hear his Voice
It would have been enough

If he had given me the opportunity to record my songs
It would have been enough

If he had dissolved with love the fears that prevented me from sharing them
It would have been enough

If after this no more songs were to come
It would have been enough

If I were to understand nothing more
It would have been enough

If tomorrow this body were to fall
It would have been enough

Because You have given me far more than it would have been reasonable to ask.

How could I not want to give back to You what I have?

I give You my voice
I give You my body
I give You my mind
I give You my marriage
I give You my work
I give You my days

So that all that belongs to the Alpha
may also belong to the Omega

And if after all this
only remained
to love in silence,
to pray,
and to labor,

It would have been enough.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 132. To Row, or Not to Row
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: Today I understand why I was wrong. A few days ago, a false and enormously influential belief was revealed and dissolved in my mind. It has to do with…
item.content:encoded:
A few days ago, a false and enormously influential belief was revealed and dissolved in my mind. It has to do with work, but above all, with the worker.

THE EXPERIMENT

At the beginning of my path, I adopted a phrase of Jesus as the thesis of what my life was going to be: "Seek first the Kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you."

The Kingdom of God is where the will of God is done; where He reigns. If there is no other will, sin cannot exist. The Kingdom is Heaven, and it is where God keeps our original innocence intact. It is, therefore, a transcendent reality, not in the future, but eternally now.

But Jesus also said that his righteousness had to be sought. In Spanish, Jesus uses the word “justice.” This is perhaps even harder to understand than the Kingdom, since it derives from It but is also in relation to this world.

After years of praying for guidance on this, I arrived at the understanding that the justice Jesus was referring to was the Justice of God. The only thing the world's justice and God's justice have in common is that both define it as "to each what is due according to their nature."

Where they differ radically is in what that nature is: the world says we are mortal sinners who deserve judgement, severe correction if not punishment or death. God says we are His Son, eternally innocent, and therefore deserve only love, which is all God gives and can give. His famous Last Judgment is an infinite and eternal "I love you, you are still as I created you."

That definition made justice also something transcendent and disembodied: remember that you are still innocent and God loves you.

The phrase of Jesus was reduced to this: Seek first the Kingdom (= your innocence) and also his righteousness (= your innocence), and all these things will be added to you.

A clear example of how human beings simplify the message of Jesus to comfortably maintain our beliefs and worldly ways. With that interpretation, all I had to do was look within and know I was loved. Having done that, I could relax and wait for "all these things to be added."

RESULTS

To that search, real but incomplete, I have dedicated these last 7 years, with considerable success, because the one who seeks finds, especially when

single-mindedly seeking something they already have eternally.

Recognizing original innocence as the only truth about myself has brought great blessings.

But, despite having recognized that inner truth, in my daily life there was still a great deal of suffering. I felt called to do something where the greatness of God would shine, but without knowing how to get there. I asked for guidance and surrendered, but nothing happened. My days were well described by the quote from Epictetus: "there can be no peace for the man who has seen what he could become."

Finally, I discovered the belief that was preventing me from moving forward: the idea that effort is unnecessary when one is in God. Everything flows with the river of existence, and it is God who acts. Everything happens easily, everything arrives miraculously.

I have spent years building a spirituality based on that.

It is not entirely false: my best songs arrived with the greatest ease. The Esferas letters often did too; after writing so many there is hardly any effort anymore. The recording of the album, for example, arrived miraculously once the blockages were undone, as if served on a silver platter.

But what about its release?

I was now being called to new and difficult things: building a community, sharing on social media, publishing my music, creating a home, a professional career. In a word: building. And building requires effort. But every time I felt resistance, I abandoned the action and fled back inward, interpreting the resistance as "I have drifted from the will, this is the ego."

In essence: when the Wind was strong, I used the billowing sails to advance without effort. But when the Wind seemed to stop, instead of rowing, I abandoned the action and turned inward, seeking to realign with Him. Not so much out of laziness, but out of fear of feeling that the Wind had disappeared.

Saint John of the Cross said: "During the time of the dryness of this night... spiritual persons suffer great trials, not so much from the aridities they endure, as from the fear of having lost their way, thinking that all spiritual good is over for them and that God has abandoned them."

THE CORRECTION

In these last few weeks, the Holy Spirit guided me to maintain a daily practice, working energetically on my solar plexus, the center of action and of "I can." All kinds of guilt, grief and shame were purged until, finally and thanks to God, the wall of pride that defended my incorrect position was brought down. As the light of truth entered, I saw my error, wept for it and for the time lost, and then it dissolved.

I now see that when the Wind disappeared, God was not asking me to abandon my action, suffer and eventually turn back to Him. He was teaching me that, even when I do not feel it, I still belong to Him and He continues to guide my actions. For this it was necessary that my soul abandon all action, saying "Father, I am not capable, take care of it yourself." Again in the words of Saint John, addressed to the soul that suffers in this way:

"Let it not be afflicted by this, but consider it a great blessing, for God is freeing it from itself and taking the matter into his own hands."

What I now see is that whether I feel the sweetness of his presence or not, my action comes from Him. If the action happens in a state of grace, I give thanks for the wind. If the action happens in pure effort, I give thanks for the strength. In either case, what drives me is always God himself.

I now see that the question is not whether effort is needed or not. The question is not whether to act or not. The question is: who is it that acts? I know that in reality there is only one will, and it is the will of God. If I am at a point in my life where it is time to lay brick upon brick, who am I to tell the Creator that, if He loves me, this should be able to happen without effort? Should I wait for gravity to disappear in order to rise, or should I go for it now with all that I’ve got?

CONCLUSION

I no longer perceive effort as the sweat of punishment presented in Genesis:

"By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread, till you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken; for you are dust, and to dust you shall return."
— Genesis 3:19

As my identification with the dust lessens, I am beginning to recognize in myself the effort of the Gospel, of the good news:

"I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me."
— Philippians 4:13

The effort is still there, always necessary while we walk through the world. But its meaning has changed for me: it no longer comes from the force of the ego, but from the strength of God shining through me.

Same reality, two different names that mark the huge difference between feeling in exile or at home.

I now see that the righteousness Jesus was referring to is not only the loving Judgment of God: it is letting Him drive me through the necessary challenges, giving me not only direction but also the strength to advance. It is ordering my life and my character according to my nature.

It is to stop resisting my destiny, which is the cause of suffering. As I stop resisting, I see that my destiny is not in my hands, and I only have to say "Yes, Lord," and lay the next brick.

In the Old Testament, the pinnacle of spiritual development was defined as being a just man: saying yes to the will of God and making it one’s law and refuge. Doing what corresponds to one's nature: if I am a painter, I paint; if I am a carpenter, I work the wood, knowing that that pleased a hidden God.

In His Words, Jesus says that to live well one must add the good news to the Old Testament. He does not abolish the law, he completes it by giving it its ultimate end: God himself. But not only discovering the Kingdom within: also living today accordingly.

Not only the Spirit; also character.

Not only the eternal; also the temporal.

Not only the true; also the good.

I now understand why Aristotle said that the ultimate goal of life was the development of character. Fifteen days ago I would have said, blind with pride, that Aristotle did not look high enough to see the true goal. Now I hear his words. I look at my life, which is a reflection of my character, and humbly recognize the path: keep working on this letter until it is finished, do the push-ups I have to do, practice piano until smoke comes out, sow, tend, make whatever efforts are required. All of that, without ever forgetting where the effort that drives me to grow comes from.

It is perfectly compatible to be in a state of grace and make a great effort. One only needs to recognize who the Doer is.

God does not abolish gravity. He gives us the strength to rise against it.

I have been called to fulfill several missions; that is my logos, my reason for being in this world, the end that guides my actions and my days.

How can I know the Logos, the ultimate reason, Christ, without first accepting my personal logos?

Now I accept it. My work is no longer only to seek God; now it is to let Him shape me: with hammer blows if I am to be a great sculpture; under great pressure if I am to be a diamond.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 131. My Voice Is Yours
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: Chronicle of a concert-liturgy. I did the sound check while the first people were beginning to enter the auditorium. When I finished, I returned to my…
item.content:encoded:
I did the sound check while the first people were beginning to enter the auditorium. When I finished, I returned to my sit, and turned inward.

Am I nervous? Not really, but there is uncertainty, I don’t know what to play. I’ve only been given ten minutes. I thought I would have more time. Normally I guide a meditation for at least 20 minutes and then play my songs. How can I condense it all? Do I skip the meditation and give a regular concert? There’s only enough time for two songs, which ones do I play? Nimbo, without a doubt, and the other one?…

This is how my mind was going as the room filled up. 400 people took their seats, laughing, greeting one another. Otman, the presenter, took the microphone, greeted everyone, and explained that the first act of the day was going to be a choreography by the team of volunteers who were helping with the event. “Music, maestro!” and the conversation of 400 people was swallowed up by party music playing at full volume. People shouted and applauded. I kept my eyes closed, searching for the calm and the Voice that had the answer to my questions. Otman then invited everyone to dance, and I watched the entire room stand up and dance around me. I remained seated, meditating. My ego said, “What are you doing! Get up and dance! Don’t you know how to enjoy yourself? You’re out of place, they’re surely looking at you and judging you: ‘Look at that guy, how spiritual…’”

Ignoring that voice afraid of social rejection, I continued sinking inward, toward silence and stillness, now with the added difficulty of being seated in the middle of a sort of nightclub. But there it was, perfect stillness, the endless space that loves us from the depths. I immersed myself there. The noisy and agitated world around me now seemed distant, as if I were diving 10 metres deep and looking at the sky through the surface. Inside me, silence.

When I arrived there, I prayed: “Holy Spirit, I don’t know what to play, I don’t know what to say or what to do. But You do. I give You my hands, my voice, my body, my brain, I give You my mind. This concert is Yours. I am Yours.”

And my mind became calm, the questions dissolved, and I calmly waited for my turn.

The music ended, Otman took the microphone again and said that something very special was coming now. He invited everyone to close their eyes, and brought their attention to their breathing and the present moment. I looked at him, he was looking at me and gestured for me to come up onto the stage. I took my guitar, went up, and standing beside him I began meditating too. In silence, he placed the microphone in front of me, gave me a pat as if saying “they’re yours,” and stepped down from the stage. My mind was in complete silence, my body in the wu chi position.

Remain with your eyes closed.

As you close your eyes, become aware that you are no longer in this room, you are in the open space of your consciousness. Within it appear the sensations of the body, different perceptions, my voice, everything floating in a dark space without limits.

Now, above your head, a sphere of energy appears.

This sphere represents, and is, All that is.

The answer to all questions, the ultimate end of every longing, everything you could possibly need, everything is in the sphere.

It has received many names throughout history: Yahweh, Brahman, wuji, God…

It is the source of your existence and, therefore, is part of you. Now we invoke it, and we are going to allow ourselves to be attuned by it. The divine substance of the sphere begins to pour over you and first floods your head, filling it with light. Your head shines like a lighthouse illuminating the room, the world, the entire universe. You are the light of the world.

The substance continues descending through the neck, shoulders, arms. It descends through the chest, flooding the heart with stillness and calm. The peace of God is in your hearts.

It continues descending through the abdomen, the pelvic area, the legs, all the way to the feet, and enters the earth.

We are all now attuned to the sphere.

The room was in perfect silence. I opened my eyes and saw that some people were crying. I closed them again, and I knew that what I am was permeating the entire room. I was the presence of light, falling through everyone’s bodies from the sphere. There was a total certainty that everyone was receiving it, even though each person registered it according to their own capacity.

I adjusted my guitar properly and began to play Nimbo.

I watched my body play, at first with its hands trembling. I heard my voice sing the first melodies with a certain care, as if feeling its way through the terrain of my body. Then, seeing that everything was in its place, the voice began to sound more confident and powerful. When I reached the chorus, the machinery of the body and the Machine Operator were one, and I felt that I was neither of them. Everything was happening by itself.

When the song ended, I raised one hand as if saying “hold the silence.” Nobody applauded, it was obvious that doing so would have stirred the waters.

Now, the divine substance, which continues falling like a waterfall through your entire body, begins to spread across the floor of the room.

The sphere is your Being, and now, by merging our energy with that of the others, we see that in reality it is the same thing, there is only one Being, there is only one sphere, and all our minds are merged in the mind of God. We are in communion.

Knowing that there is no separation between your mind and that of the others, and knowing that each one of your thoughts has an effect on the others, I invite you to bring a loving thought into the room, something that you would like to give as a gift to all your brothers and sisters gathered here.

The intensity of the joy multiplied instantly. More people crying, knowing themselves embraced by 400 souls finally recognizing that there is no separation.

In that silence saturated with light, I began to play Known = Loved.

Any insecurity that may have been present at the beginning had already dissolved here. In a state of total surrender, I felt and heard my voice fly freely throughout my entire range. It sounded with such power that, at the climax of the song, I felt that my voice was not being produced by my body, but was an emanation of the very space of the room.

I finished the song feeling my instrument reach its limit:

I am the Love that howls in the night
I am the Love that longs for your eyes
I am the Love that holds you in spite of all the ways in which you feel you don’t deserve to be loved

After that final and long verse, sung a cappella, silence.

My entire body reverberated with such intense energy that I had to project it downward, like a grounding wire redirecting a lightning bolt.

10 seconds of silence, tears, and faces of recollection.

You may open your eyes.

I had planned to play one more song, but the entire room erupted in applause. Whistles. Everyone on their feet.

I remained as if still meditating, receiving the intensity of that ovation. I moved away from the microphone, bowed, and thanked them. I raised one hand pointing toward the sky, redirecting the applause toward the One who deserved our gratitude.

The applause continued, and I placed my hand on my heart to thank them again. There, beneath my shirt, I felt my crucifix. I took it out, and it shone like a star on my chest in the light of the spotlights.

Nacho, the organiser of the event, came up onto the stage and said “when I see Antonio I see God”

He gave me a hug. The applause continued. I thanked them again and stepped down from the stage.

On my way to my seat, several people approached me to give me hugs. I gave them hugs, happy. As I embraced their bodies, I brought my attention to their hearts, and then silently showed them the context of their existence, the infinite Being that is in the whole universe.

After several minutes like this giving hugs like these, I reached my seat, sat down, closed my eyes and gave thanks.

Only then did I realize that at no point had I introduced myself. What a disaster! my ego said.

But I smiled thinking: “Well, I suppose this wasn’t about me. And perhaps that’s better this way, the Holy Spirit knows what He is doing”

And so it was. Not saying my name meant that the people who really wanted to get to know me and my work came up to me. I spoke with several of them, who said things like

“Thank you from the heart, what you did went right through me” or “It had been a long time since I had experienced the presence of the Holy Spirit. Thank you!” or “Thank you for stepping out of the way.”

Another greeted me saying “The voice of God!”

Inside me, I continued holding the finger pointed upward.

Telling all of this is an exercise in daring to express with true openness how I experience life. I have been given an immense gift, one that loses its value when hidden, and multiplies when given away.

Now I understand better what I have been looking for: birds sing not to achieve anything, but because they are what they are.

I am what I am, and I must sing my truth. Let nothing remain unsaid.

With all my love,

Antonio

P.D. I have become the person whose help I desperately needed four years ago, when my heart opened, reality burst into my mind, and my human psyche collapsed. If there is someone else out there going through that, they will only be able to find me if I speak openly. I am offering 1:1 sessions, a structure to hold the chaos and accompany people on the journey.

You can book one here

item.title: 130. Evet
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: Story of a calling. This week I said an "Evet" ("yes" in Turkish) that, joined with another "Evet," founded a family.
item.content:encoded:
This week I said an "Evet" ("yes" in Turkish) that, joined with another "Evet," founded a family.

Almost four years ago, my heart opened, and everything changed radically and permanently. Relationships, purpose, perception, sense of identity... everything was transformed overnight.

Around that time, I was a regular at a yoga studio. One day I met a beautiful monk who would become one of my closest friends from my Boston years, Father Bon. He invited me to his monastery to help him clean out the goat shed. Once there, another friend of his appeared, another beautiful man named Jay. He too quickly became a fundamental friend in my life there.

We spent the morning among rakes, sawdust and wheelbarrows, followed by tea and a pleasant conversation about the religious icons that lined the walls.

When we finished, Jay offered to drive me home, and I accepted gratefully.

I told him I was going through a very hard and confusing time, which I called the "opening of my heart."

He told me he had been through the same thing, which surprised me enormously because I had never heard anyone speak of anything similar, and here I was in a car with someone who understood. It was a relief to know that the psychedelic storm I was living through was in fact an archetypal process.

He described it like this: the chakra system is like a river. A closed heart is like a part of the river where a large log has fallen and is blocking the flow. Behind that log other things get stuck, and gradually something like a dam forms. But if the water in the river begins to push and push harder, it can eventually break the log apart. When that happens, not only does the flow of the river increase enormously, but for a time it also carries along all kinds of things that had been stuck until then.

There was an explanation for my emotional storm, and also for the intense spiritual experiences I had been having.

Afterward, having already arrived at my place, he stopped right in front, made a sudden leap in the conversation, and began telling me how he had met his wife.

I will leave out the story out of respect for his privacy. I will only say that it was a hero's journey that passed through where I was now and ended in marriage. A process I also recognized as archetypal, and which I therefore received as a prophecy, or a map that Jay was handing me for my own adventure.

The doubts about whether I should go to a monastery had been resolved a few days earlier. The Voice that speaks for God answered clearly: "No, your path is in the world."

Now, that same spirit of truth finished the message through Jay: "and therefore, you will start a family."

"Jay, you can't imagine how much everything you've just told me..." and he, looking at me calmly, said with tenderness: "I know, I know." I then stopped explaining myself because I could see he knew perfectly well what I was going through. I threw myself to hug him. I understood in that moment that, after spending several weeks praying ardently for some clarity on this matter of intimate relationships, it had finally arrived. Jay had appeared in my life, and without my asking or even mentioning the subject, he had given me exactly the clarity I was looking for. God had answered my prayers with miraculous force. Jay understood it that way too and said "I suppose this encounter was meant to be."

Still in shock, I got out of his car. He got out too and gave me a proper hug. Hugging someone with such an open heart is a completely different experience from an ordinary hug. As our chests came together, through our clothes and coats, I felt his heart and mine entering into a conversation. In that energetic exchange, my newly opened and frightened heart met a heart that was open and at peace, and that peace communicated itself to mine. At the risk of diminishing the inexpressible depth of that exchange, if it had happened in words it would have gone something like this:

— I am suffering a great deal and I am afraid, but what you have just shared with me and your mere presence comfort me tremendously.
— I know. I know what you are going through. Hold on, you are doing well, I am here with you for whatever you need. There is a deep and luminous peace that you will see when the waters calm.

We said goodbye, I thanked him again and went upstairs. I went straight to my room, collapsed to my knees in front of my altar and wept loudly for several minutes, giving thanks for what had just happened. It was the deep weeping of a man who recognizes himself as safe and loved in God's hands. The weeping of someone who recognizes unequivocally what he truly wants in this world of confusion, conflict and disordered desires. The weeping of a son of divorced parents who recognizes that marriage is not a fallible invention of man, but a vocation that comes from God and goes toward Him. I felt the relief of the sailor who sees a guiding star appear through the storm clouds: my path was marriage.

There was still much journey ahead, a year of darkness that ended, as Jay's story had prophesied, with total surrender: "Lord, if you want me to remain single forever, so be it." Only then did I finally recognize that the love I had spent my whole life searching for out there had always been present at the bottom of my heart. It was the love of Christ, like a lake of infinite depth and eternally unfailing.

Two days later my relationship with Betül began.

This week I married her.

Gloria in excelsis Deo!

With all my love,

Antonio

P.D.: Thank you, Father, for the good friends who help us find our way.

item.title: 129. You Are NOW
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: Do you know your true value? What is it that is valuable?, you say as you fix on my eye your celestial eye. What is it that is valuable? And you ask me…
item.content:encoded:
What is it that is valuable?, you say as you fix

on my eye your celestial eye.

What is it that is valuable? And you ask me this?

What is valuable... is you.

This morning I pulled on the thread:

I feel overwhelmed by everything I have to do.

And what happens if you don't do it?

Then the people I work with will think I am sloppy.

And what happens if they think that?

I will feel depressed.

Why?

Because I will feel worthless.

There it is. Stop.

That fear of being worthless is not something that will appear in the future if everything else goes wrong. It is a belief about yourself that is active right now behind the curtain of your conscious mind, influencing everything you do. The pressure you feel to do things comes from there, from that fear of being worthless, from that self that feels insufficient.

Let us question that.

According to the world's value system, our worth is measured by what we have or by what we do. A person is valuable if they have a lot of money, followers, status, connections, an aesthetic body, shiny objects... Or if they do admirable things: they are productive, diligent, athletic, have an interesting and high-impact job... As my friend Juan used to say when we were children, laughing at the values the world was beginning to instill in us: "the most important thing is to be really hot."

Nothing wrong with those values, by the way. In general, they come from legitimate human needs. They are part of the daily bread: having health, a decent livelihood, feeling that we contribute to the world or that we belong to a community. I am not saying, therefore, that the path is to renounce these human realities. What I want to bring to light in this letter is: are you letting those external and highly variable things dictate whether you are valuable or not?

What the world tends to overlook is the value that comes from what we are, and that is where our true dignity and sense of fullness are born.

When we lose contact with what we essentially are, a void is created that nothing in the world can fill. But we try anyway, using having and doing to compensate for that apparently empty, small and insufficient self. From there, we will want to do things well, and that is good. But the fuel behind our actions will be fear; the fear that the world will discover that, in reality, we are not good or valuable or worthy of being loved.

How can we resolve that underlying fear and sense of insufficiency?

We will have to ask the One who knows who we truly are, and what our true value is. We did not create ourselves; God is our Creator, and only He knows perfectly what we are. When we doubt our worth, instead of looking outward and seeking an answer in this mad world, let us turn inward and ask:

Who are we? Show us our value and our identity as You know us.

This morning I asked that question in communion with Betül, and the answer came in this form:

You are NOW.

That answer was not merely a thought. It came with a profoundly liberating shift in perspective: my sense of identity was no longer in my body; rather, I was the sphere of consciousness aware of itself, within which the body, Betül, the entire park and everything else appeared.

You are NOW.

From there I saw that I am no more the body of Antonio than that of Betül, or the tree growing beside us. Our true identity is not different from the eternal NOW that watches the changing world pass by.

From that identity, beyond space and time, one can say: "Before Abraham was, I am."

Betül then rested her head on my shoulder and I felt the love that had inspired that gesture, as well as the love it awakened in me.

You are that love, and there is only one love and it is the love of God.

The question about our intrinsic value was transformed then into:

How much is the love of God worth?

How much is NOW worth?

And a great flock of birds flew past between clouds filled with rain and light.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 128. Vacation at the Mechanic's
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: Today's teacher was a flat tire. Some are traveling in exotic places. Others are in the city with the AC on. All equally fortunate, because the Truth is…
item.content:encoded:
Some are traveling in exotic places.

Others are in the city with the AC on.

All equally fortunate, because the Truth is with everyone.

After a couple of months without leaving the concrete maze that is Istanbul, yesterday we got in the car and drove to spend a few days by the sea.

The first thing we did when we arrived was get a flat tire.

We would have preferred to spend the time among pine trees and waves, but God arranged for the first morning to unfold among tow trucks and wheel rims.

While we waited for the mechanic to arrive, I asked Betül how she was feeling. She said frustrated, that this is not what she would choose to be doing with her short vacation. We began to explore that perspective and remembered that every form of suffering comes from a mistaken perception. We prayed together:

"Holy Spirit, help us to see this with love. We let go of whatever interpretation we were holding. Show us the truth of this situation."

A few minutes later, I opened my eyes and saw that Betül was smiling. I asked her what she had received:

"Everything is perfect."

I then shared what came to me, which given the way my mind works, brought the same message but more elaborated (some of us need things explained in more detail):

We believe that vacation should be a time without problems, free from the mundane burdens and tasks that follow us around the city. So when the tire went flat the moment we arrived, that event seemed to go completely against what was supposed to be happening. Hence the frustration.

But when I let go of that human construct of "vacation versus ordinary life," what I saw was that true rest does not come from being near the sea or reading under a parasol. True rest comes from showing up to whatever is going on with love, because then we allow God to carry us. In other words, what exhausts us is resisting what is happening, and rest comes from surrendering lovingly.

The real joy, rest and peace were not at the beach, but in lovingly accompanying each other through the adventure of changing a tire in 90-degree heat.

If Jesus were the third person in the car, how would he hold the situation? How would he treat the mechanic? How would he treat us, and how would he treat himself?

(The truth is I would trade every vacation for the rest of my life for one morning at the mechanic with Jesus.)

The key is that Christ is always present. It is enough to honestly say "Yes, Father," and then go about whatever needs to be done with tenderness, joy and diligence.

And so it was.

A couple of hours later, the whole thing sorted out, Betül and I were in a state of joy that could only have come from the Heaven within us. I said to her: "Do you remember the prayer this morning? Eight words: 'Holy Spirit, help us to see this with love,' and the course of the morning changed radically: from a wasted morning to a beautiful one."

"Wow," she said.

"Wow," I said.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 127. Battle for My Mind
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: Is there a demon in my aura?... Yes. Encouraged by the members of my community, Between Heaven and Earth, I am finally sharing a letter I wrote during my…
item.content:encoded:
Encouraged by the members of my community, Between Heaven and Earth, I am finally sharing a letter I wrote during my last semester at Berklee, and never dared to send.

Yesterday, around 3 in the afternoon, I decided to do a qigong practice that consists of meditating standing up, holding different postures for several minutes each. That is what the body does, but the real work is in the mind. It begins with the visualization of a sphere of light a few centimeters above the head. It is a large sphere, about a meter in diameter, and it represents wuji, the Chinese name for "All that is." This sphere contains everything, all that was, all that is and will be; all the answers, all intelligence, all love and power. It is a hologram of totality, and it shares all the qualities of the divine. For the first 15 minutes, one concentrates on this sphere.

When the bell sounds, attention moves to the center of the Earth, where one visualizes a large golden sphere. This is the energy or essence of Mother Nature. For 15 minutes, one connects with this center and, with each inhalation, pumps this golden energy upward through the legs, storing it in the abdomen.

The third part consists of fusing these two spheres in the abdomen, so for 15 minutes, the inhalation draws both spheres toward the navel, and on the exhale they return each to their position, above and below. This practice is designed for one to merge with Heaven and Earth, becoming a bridge between the two. In Christian terms, it would be an energetic training in "Thy Will be done on Earth as it is in Heaven."

Two minutes into the practice, a fight broke out in the street below my window. I recognized one of the people involved by her voice, more like a dog's bark than a human voice. The poor woman has one of the most unpleasant and powerful voices I have ever heard. And this time, she was screaming at two or three other people in the street. The argument escalated to a point where I would not have been surprised if it had ended in gunfire. The energy was terrible. And simultaneously, there I was, standing motionless like a tree, inhaling the energy of Heaven and Earth. It did not seem coincidental, and I decided to intervene. I expanded my aura not only upward and downward, but outward toward the street, trying to envelop the situation with the energy of "let there be peace."

I felt as though I were extending an embrace toward them and, in doing so, something terrible entered my aura. This was to be expected: they were fighting, not praying the rosary together. So I held tight to my connection with Heaven and Earth, and also connected the aura of the people involved to the Earth, so that the discordant energy could be neutralized through grounding.

It was an exercise in maintaining internal peace in the presence of terrible energy. I did it with considerable success and, after a few minutes, the fight dissolved.

When the practice ended I felt recharged and at peace. But something stayed with me, because as the afternoon advanced I began to feel worse. I had planned to begin my last practice of the day at 7pm, but an enormous resistance appeared and I spent almost an hour watching YouTube shorts. When I saw it was already 8, I put down my phone and closed my eyes. I observed my body and my mind, dulled by so much noise. I was surprised to find there was no guilt or any other emotion, only white noise. It was a very strange sensation, a suspicious neutrality. I almost felt as though I had no soul.

I began my evening practice, called Old Man Tide Pool. It is designed to purge emotional energies, and it is very powerful. I am doing it for 40 days, and that was night 25. I did it, and purged some energetic blockages that gradually brought me back to a more familiar place: ah, my soul has returned. Some joy, some courage... something!

I finished the practice around 9:15pm and felt I should meditate. I sat down and, the moment I observed my energy, I felt something very unsettling. I asked: "Is there a demon in my aura?" And the answer was: "Yes."

And so began a battle for my mind that would not end until 36 hours later.

The first thing I did was reconnect with the sphere above my head and let it fall over my body, invoking and attuning my aura to the energy of Heaven. Every time I had experienced a similar encounter before, that is what I did, and it always worked to expel whatever malign presence had come to visit. I did it, and felt enormous resistance. My body, possessed, began to growl and heave in a terrifying way. I held tight to the sphere until that wave of dark energy passed. But I could sense something was still there.

"Is there still something in my aura?"

"Yes."

I invoked Jesus Christ and the energy stirred violently. I leapt to my feet, sensing I would need far more power than I could summon sitting down. I spent an hour standing, sweating, invoking the light and expelling demons from my aura.

"IN THE NAME OF JESUS CHRIST, LET THERE BE LIGHT"

"ARCHANGEL SAINT MICHAEL, DEFEND ME IN BATTLE!"

"ONLY LIGHT IS WELCOME HERE!"

The demonic energy passed through me, contorting my body in the most terrifying ways. It growled and resisted the light, clinging to my mind with its claws. It also laughed and mocked me and my invocations. It came in strong waves and, after each one, I would ask again, always with the same answer.

"Is there still something in my aura?"

"Yes."

I thought about calling Joe, knowing there is no darkness that can withstand the magnitude of his light. But at the same time, I felt called to face this alone. I saw in this massive attack a golden opportunity to elevate myself, to clear my mind of vulnerabilities and reclaim the power God wants for me.

Two ideas came to mind to inspire me:

No attack or challenge on the path is too great. But sometimes it can catch you at a moment when you do not feel strong enough to face it. There lies the opportunity for growth: the ego finds itself completely overwhelmed and ultimately has no choice but to ask for divine intervention and step aside.

The second idea is that these malign entities feed on vulnerable minds. If they were now in my mind, it was because there was something in me they could hold on to. I understood it had to do with the fear I had of them. Sooner or later I would have to cross through and release that fear of demons, and this was the opportunity.

It is not possible to return to the light without passing through the darkness. The path to God passes necessarily through hell, and it is there that one faces these things in order to resolve vulnerabilities. And so the truth was restored, coming to me in this moment of need through these words from A Course in Miracles:

Nothing real can be threatened.
Nothing unreal exists.
Therein lies the peace of God.

What I truly am, the Self, is like a cinema screen: whatever happens in the film cannot affect the screen itself. Only from that point of observation can one see that there is truly nothing to fear, that one is eternally safe.

I already knew that "place," I had experienced it on numerous occasions, but my mind still oscillated between that and identification with the character. In the film, Antonio was fighting with all his strength against demons. In the Self, there is no problem, and one can see that everything is in God's hands.

The battle began on Saturday night, and I called on all my strength to deal with the situation. I intuitively embodied the archetype of the spiritual warrior: something like a Jedi.

But my body, after several nights of poor sleep and two hours of fighting on my feet, was beginning to feel very tired. I knew something was still hidden in my aura, and I was terrified of going to sleep and leaving my dreams in its hands. But I saw no other option, so I went to bed, made the sign of the cross, and surrendered to God, falling immediately into a restless sleep.

Fortunately, there were no terrible nightmares or unpleasant experiences. I woke tired, but no more than the days before. I knew something was still there when I noticed an enormous resistance to doing my morning practices. What normally draws me in and gives me peace now repelled me. The battle began again, and I called once more on the Jedi within. But it was not enough, and the struggle was exhausting. It genuinely felt like taking a physical beating.

I remembered reading about Padre Pio expressing similar experiences, unable to understand how a non-physical entity could have the capacity to harm the body. Now I was living it: it is not that these demons take physical form and beat you; the attack occurs at the level of the mind, and the mind controls the body. So when, for example, I invoked Archangel Michael and the light entered my mind, that dark energy expressed itself through my body as though it were its own, contorting in violent ways, emitting growls mixed with macabre laughter. In short, the body was only the battlefield, and the two sides, light and darkness, were fighting for my mind.

Seen from outside, my body was like a marionette in the hands of two quarreling puppeteers. Meanwhile, in my mind, I was using all my tools and watching the malign presence distort them. If I invoked the luminous sphere above my head, what appeared was a black hole. If I directed the celestial substance of the sphere to cover and purify my body, what fell was a cascade of blood. Everything I did was transformed into something horrible.

But on this second day of battle, I began to understand something. What I truly am is love, which is simply the fact that everything is one. By positioning myself as a warrior in the battle, I was separating myself from my enemy, perpetuating the dance of opposites. Seeing this, I began to rise until I could see that, in reality, the demon is part of me, and love unites me to it as much as to Antonio. That is the vision of Christ, and it had such an effect that I thought, after one final shudder, the malign presence had gone.

But no. I still felt as though the sky were overcast. There was no joy, and it was hard to look with love. That is how I spent the rest of Sunday, and my evening practices were not much more effective.

What did happen was that, little by little, the fear began to dissolve. I understood that, for my invocation of God's power to truly take effect, I had to get out of the way. That meant that, in the middle of a demonic attack, instead of positioning myself as a Jedi warrior, I should present myself as defenseless and vulnerable as a child: a child who trusts completely in the protecting arms of his Father.

I also knew that, even though I was now going through a difficult moment, the happy outcome was certain. Everything is in God's hands, and there was not the slightest doubt in me that sooner or later, this passage through hell would end.

So, instead of fighting, I began to relax more and more, and to welcome everything. And I began to discover that true invulnerability lies in total defenselessness. "Do not resist the evil one; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also" [Matthew 5:38-39]. These words not only began to make sense, but appeared as the only way that made any sense at all.

On Monday morning, still walking with this dark cloud hovering in my mind, I thought: "Two nights ago, when this began, I saw it as an opportunity to grow. But who was it that thought that? Obviously the ego. So why not ask Joe for help?"

I finally allowed myself to do so and sent him a message explaining the situation.

A few minutes later, two ideas passed through my mind:

"Faith is mental fortitude" and "Say the word and I shall be healed."

These words passed through my mind like a sunbeam and I felt the demonic energy disappear in a breathless exhalation.

I sensed my mind was clean again when, passing in front of a church, I felt the desire to go in. I sat in a pew at the back. It was a large, dark, silent and peaceful space. Three people were praying and I sat down to do the same.

After a while, one of them stood up, knelt, and as he turned around I saw it was my friend Julian. He came over, gave me a hug and asked how I was. I told him it had been one of the hardest weekends of my life. He looked at me and said: "How can I pray for you?"

The question surprised me. No one had ever asked me that. I stayed quiet, searching for an answer. But what came was another question: "Who are you?"

"Pardon?" he said, confused.

"Sorry, I know you are Julian, but that is not what I was asking. I was invoking the light in you, because seeing it reminds me of it in myself."

"Oh, okay!" he said, understandably puzzled. He gave me a hug and left.

I sat back down, and now, grateful and moved, I knew I had made it to the other side.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 126. Sandcastles
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: What survives the tide? There are many kinds of sandcastles: large, small, built by children's hands, by architects' hands, some swept away quickly by the…
item.content:encoded:
There are many kinds of sandcastles: large, small, built by children's hands, by architects' hands, some swept away quickly by the tide, others lasting weeks, and in the end all of them surrendering to entropy. Forms that appear, endure for a time, and dissolve. But the sand, the substance, that remains.

At the Council of Nicaea (325 AD), the Creed was drawn up, describing the divine filiation of Jesus Christ by saying that He and the Father are of the same substance. Saint John also opens his gospel speaking of how Christ is the creative principle of the Universe.

Christ is the sand of which the Universe is made. But unlike sand, he is not an inert substance. He is consciousness itself, the light that illuminates the world and allows you to know it in this instant. He is the subjective element, that constant "I" at the center of your experience that wisdom calls us to investigate.

And then, here we are, you and I: human beings of flesh and blood, with a screen in front of us, sitting here in a world that appears to be made of matter. We are sandcastles that are born, change, and dissolve. At this level we give ourselves names: Antonio, Juan, Betül, Jesus... names that seem to encapsulate that "I" inside a body. Everything outside the body is not "me."

But when one closes one's eyes and investigates that "I" in depth, it does not take long to discover that, in reality, it does not refer to the castle but to the sand. Essentially we are sand: the consciousness that is at once unchanging and the substance of the changing world.

The only difference between Jesus and us is that when Jesus said "I," he was referring exclusively to the sand. He accepted nothing temporal, nothing subject to entropy, as a limitation of his identity. He stayed only with the eternal, fully accepting his divine nature as the Son consubstantial with the Father. That does not mean he rejected his human nature. On the contrary, it reached its fullest expression in that boundless I.

The question is: who are you and I? Are we the castles, or are we the sand?

If I say I am the castle, I have chosen to identify with the body. That is the ego, faithful believer in the god of separation, which tells me that at the end of this limited life death awaits. The one who puts his mind in service of the ego sees only castles, and the wars and romances that play out among their inhabitants. The one who looks that way never notices the omnipresence of the sand.

But if I say I am the sand, I have chosen to believe in the God of Jesus, and then death is just one more change, not an ending. I still see the castles, but they are no longer defined by their variable forms, only by the one sand. The one who looks this way sees only Christ. The tide will come and carry the castle away, but the sand remains.

In saying I am the sand, I am no longer looking at the human body with which I tend to identify. I am looking at the substance of which my entire experience in this moment is made. There are other people in my experience now. I am writing from an airplane. I hear a baby crying, the morning light comes through the windows: clouds, blue sky, the Mediterranean Sea, all made of the sand of consciousness, all "I," all radiant Christ.

The body of Antonio appears, changes over years, and one day will disappear. The same will happen with the voice that sounds in my mind and claims to be me. But that voice is not me. It is only a name written in the sand, a strange poem about time fears, longings, and blueberries. Castles. Forms that arise and dissolve. But what remains? The sand, consciousness, the timeless I that we share with Jesus and with the Father.

Jesus told us: Deny yourself.

He also invited us to pray saying: Hallowed be Thy name (referring to the Father).

Both ideas converge: I am the eternal sand, not the temporary castle.

Cleanse your name, your sense of "I," from what appears in your experience. That comes and goes. But I am always I. Stay only with what remains. Return to the recognition that eternal life is already here, and it is you, dressed up as time.

The body will still be yours, but now it will be guided by an integrated mind, not a divided one. Your daily life will be guided by the Holy Spirit, not by Legion.

Your steps through this world will write a love poem in the sand, a call to the other castles to recognize: you are me. And when the tide carries the castle away, nothing essential will have changed, nothing essential will have been lost. The sand will remain. The Son, at last without disguise, will open his eyes again to the happy face of the Father.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 125. The Agent
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: What is your responsibility, and what is not? To contemplate Nature, you don't need to go out into the fields. Just observe yourself, without judgment…
item.content:encoded:
To contemplate Nature, you don't need to go out into the fields. Just observe yourself, without judgment. For a moment, try looking at your body not as "me," but in the way you look at a cloud or a flower.

Who is directing the chemical processes happening in your body right now?

Who is running your organs?

Who is directing the synapses that decide you next thought?

Who heals the wounds in the skin? And the ones in the soul?

Who decided to read this letter?

Who is doing the breathing?

Who decides to relax the forehead and shoulders?

Who is responsible for moving your eyelids?

Who is responsible for everything else you do throughout the day?

The one who chooses the food, cuts it, chews it and digests it, is it always the same agent, or does it change?

Who is at the controls of your life?

Who decides what happens in it? What words you say, who you run into, what you decide to buy, when you decide to pray, when sleep comes over you, when you wake up...

Who draws the line between what is under your control and what is not?

Who decides what you are responsible for, and what you are not?

The ego is the thought that interprets what happens as "I did this, this is me, I am guilty of this, responsible for that, and if I don't do it, it will go undone."

Meanwhile, the heart keeps beating, the photon keeps traveling, the lotus keeps opening, the musician keeps composing, and the baby keeps forming.

With all my love,

Antonio

item.title: 124. You Are With Me
item.dc:creator: Antonio de Arcas
item.description: Founding a monastery of two. Almost four years ago, my heart opened to a more direct communication with God. It was a period so difficult and profound…
item.content:encoded:
Almost four years ago, my heart opened to a more direct communication with God. It was a period so difficult and profound that I felt the moment had come to leave for a monastery. But the Voice, which always speaks through all things, told me clearly: no, my path was to remain in the world and start a family.

Almost three years ago, Betül came into my life. Our relationship began in Boston. She was studying at Harvard and her lab was a seven-minute bike ride from my apartment, so we spent a lot of time together. Coming from Turkey and Spain respectively, the United States gave us the opportunity to create our own culture, tailored to both of us.

The heart of that culture was silence, which from the very beginning accompanied us on our dates and wrapped itself around our conversations. This silence was unusual, neither uncomfortable nor empty: it was filled with peace and felt strangely familiar. That helped me recognize, very early in our relationship, that she was the person I was going to marry. In that silence I would look at her thinking: "here we are, two strangers, united by a mysterious peace that can only come from God. It is like an arranged marriage, but arranged not by our parents, but by God himself."

A few months later, she began to feel curious about that enormous book I read every morning: A Course in Miracles. She came from Islam, but as she gradually came to know what was in my heart, she began to feel that call that Jesus makes not only through truth, but primarily through affection. Shortly after, without me saying a word, she picked up the book and did the first lesson. That was how we began our shared contemplative practice. The peace we had already been sensing took on the name of Christ, and without realizing it, we founded a monastery of two.

A year and a half ago she finished her PhD at Harvard and returned to her native Istanbul. The morning after dropping her at the airport, her absence in my apartment was like a silent thunderclap. I threw myself fully into that emptiness and, like Gandalf seizing his sword as he fell against the Balrog, I took up the sword of truth and launched myself against loneliness. The account of that battle is in my letter "61. Love and Attachment. Sky and Clouds."

What I did not tell in that letter was that, in defeating the monster of loneliness, my mind opened to the fact that loneliness is, in reality, impossible. I already knew that my consciousness was non-local, but now I accepted it as my everyday reality. For that reason, I never fully experienced what a long-distance relationship actually is. The year and a half that followed her departure we have enjoyed a non-local relationship, one in which we recognize that our presence is not limited by space. That omnipresent presence, always perfectly comforting, which never let us be overcome by loneliness or the sense of separation, was Christ himself shining in our hearts.

She calls me canim, "darling" in Turkish. I call her the same. And we both know that, in reality, canim is the light in the other, and there is only one light.

That recognition led us beyond the classic "I love you," and we began using the phrase "you are me." It says the same thing, but strips from the expression everything that looks like love and in reality is not.

One day, Betül went a step further, by accident. Wanting to express, from Istanbul to Madrid, that presence which transcends space, she tried to say "you are with me" in Spanish. But instead of saying "estás conmigo" she said "eres conmigo." "Estás” is a reference to being somewhere, bur “Eres” refers to pure being. You are with me, not here or there, but in being. You are me.

That is the rock on which Jesus is teaching us to build. A love cultivated in the cross, in forgiveness, in the yes to the storm that leads to the transcendence of conflict and separation. A love not based on emotion, not subject to space or time. It includes without exception, and eternally, every living being. So I apply the phrase not only to Betül, but also to you who are reading this: eres conmigo.

With all my love,

Antonio
